While the petitioner was working as Senior Inspector under the Directorate of Fruit and Vegetable Preservation under the Ministry of Food Processing Industries, the employees working there were transferred to Food, Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI), as per Ext.P3 order dated 25.11.2008, under Section 90 of the FSS Act, on the very same conditions of service.

entities.label: ORG

entities.text: Food, Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Though those employees were given opportunity to give option to go back to the Ministry on expiry of 6 months,
the petitioner did not opt for that.

While continuing in FSSAI in the re-designated post of Assistant Director, the 4th respondent issued Ext.P7 order on 26.03.2012, calling for option and ordered that those joining FSSAI would be on deemed deputation and would be governed by Rule 37A of the CCS(Pension) Rules, contrary to the terms of transfer under Section 90 of the Act.
The petitioner was thereafter repatriated to the parent Ministry on 31.03.2015, and much after that he was redeployed in the CBDT.

The petitioner now claims that option called for in Ext.P7 was not legal, as the respondents themselves have in Ext.P9 order dated 10.03.2017, found that on transfer to FSSAI,
the employees were eligible for benefits under Section 90 of the Act.
The petitioner claims that he has submitted Ext.P11 representation requesting to re-post him in FSSAI, as Ext.P7 order as well as option obtained under it were without authority.
2. The learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner would be satisfied with a direction to the respondents to consider Ext.P10 representation.

In view of the limited relief sought for, the writ petition is disposed of directing the 2nd respondent to consider and pass orders on Ext.P10 representation within a period of two months from the date of receipt of a copy of the judgment.

Sd/-
(P.V.ASHA, JUDGE) rtr/
